headline: Should I Choose an Attached ADU for My Home?
articleBody:
Deciding whether an attached Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU) is the right move for your Los Angeles home involves weighing several factors unique to this type of build. An attached ADU means the new living space shares at least one wall with your existing home. This can be a fantastic way to add significant value and functionality without taking up precious backyard space, making it perfect for smaller lots in areas like West Hollywood or Marina Del Rey. 

Attached ADUs are often more cost-effective to build than detached units because they can share existing utilities and sometimes even parts of the foundation or roofing. This integration can also make the permitting process a bit smoother. It's an ideal solution if you're looking to create a seamless extension of your home for a growing family, a private space for live-in care, or a rental unit that feels connected yet distinct. We've helped many homeowners in Glendale, Pasadena, and Encino achieve this balance. 

However, it's important to consider how the new space will integrate with your current home's layout and privacy. Our design-build team specializes in creating thoughtful solutions that maintain your home's architectural integrity and maximize comfort for both occupants. We'll work through the design to ensure it feels like a natural part of your home, not just an add-on.
